# One-pulse Kerr: coherent count CDF classical attack

13 November2026. Selected after STATE/TRAPS, corpus been-tried/baselines,
actual Hiary theorem and retained quantum primary statements, and full201LF
independent comparison with isogeny vectorization/Jones normalization.
No classical polynomial sampler is established. Known quantum endpoint and
small-numerical-period classical sampler remain unchanged.

## Native question and candidate

Binary K, two rational-turn passive angles theta1,theta2, rational a/b,
0<epsilon<=1/4. Start |K,0>, apply B(theta1), exp(2pi i(a/b)binom(N,2)),
B(theta2), and sample one output count in {0,...,K} within epsilon TV.
All angle/phase bits, log(K+1), error and output bits count. The known quantum
endpoint is polynomial in native bits,logK,log1epsilon. Seek a classical
match polynomial in native bits,logK,1/epsilon (a polylog error clock would
be stronger). No smoothing, finite-window oracle, physical exponential-photon
source, hidden state or postselection is supplied.

Mechanism to test: replace the full rotated number-prefix projector by its
exact rank-two DISPLACEMENT/Christoffel-Darboux description; compile the
resulting chirped-binomial quadratic form with certified weighted theta sums.
This attacks the SAME count law and preserves off-diagonal interference.
Strong baselines: direct K+1 evolution; passive/binomial and terminal-Kerr
cases; coherent finite-revival-branch rejection in numerical2b, already proved
in BINARY_FOCK_KERR_SAMPLING.md. Rational approximation alone does not give
poly(logK): denominators can remain of order sqrt(K). No missing comparator,
large Hilbert space or large denominator is hardness evidence.

## Exact identities checked by the parent

Let U=B(theta2) in number coordinates, N=diag(0,...,K), Pi_r the number-prefix
projector, P_r=U^T Pi_r U, and w_n the first rotated binomial amplitude times
the exact Kerr phase. F(r)=w*P_r w. T=U N U^T is tridiagonal. For0<=r<K,
t_r=T[r,r+1], u=U^T e_r,v=U^T e_(r+1):

 [N,P_r]=t_r(vu^T-uv^T),
 P_r[n,m]=t_r(v_n u_m-u_n v_m)/(n-m), n!=m.

P_r still has rankr+1; this is not a low-rank projector. Its diagonal is a
separate confluent CD expression with polynomial derivatives. The exact
Fourier integral for1/(n-m) is not an efficient integration rule.
The classical target is a certified compiler for F(r), uniformly in prefix,
angles, rational phase and K. If it costs poly(logK,anglebits,log1delta),
quantile search at delta=epsilon/[8(K+1)] with a similarly fine uniform
variate gives TV error<=epsilon/2 by coupling outside all CDF-boundary bands.
Only O(logK) queries are needed. O(epsilon) Kolmogorov error is insufficient.
Full201LF proof/selection: audits/reviews/2026-11-13-post-witt-selection.md.

## Actual source boundaries

Hiary Annals2011 Theorem1.1 (actual PDF/text retained under
sources/2026-11-13-one-pulse/) evaluates
K^-j sum_(k=0)^K k^j exp(2pi i(alpha*k+beta*k^2)), REAL alpha,beta mod1,
with arithmetic/operand bits polynomial in nu=(j+1)log(K/eta) and output
error A1*nu^kappa1*eta. Parent read theorem and algorithm scope. Its
arbitrary constants are constructive proof constants, not a supplied numeric
implementation certificate. Gaussian damping, Krawtchouk weights, confluent
diagonal and bilinear Cauchy-kernel sum are NOT included automatically.
Actual DLMF18.2.12/13 supply CD/confluent identities,18.23.3 the Krawtchouk
generating identity. The parent independently derived the displayed matrix
identity. No efficient algorithm follows from that algebra.
Dai-Wong global Krawtchouk source was NOT obtained: CiteSeer returned429 and
author mirror403/nonPDF. Abstracts are not an imported uniform error theorem;
any such theorem must be fetched/read or replaced by a direct derivation.

## Proof obligations and falsifiers

Pay a polynomial number of weighted-sum pieces, their degree and coefficient
bits, all cancellations, diagonal evaluation, integration and all-branch
clocks. Needed accuracy includes delta=epsilon/O(K), so a polynomial cost in
1/delta is not a native polynomial compiler. Central binomial truncation
alone leaves sqrt(K) terms. Bulk asymptotics do not cover turning points,
coalescing saddles, nearly trivial rotations or near-rational revivals.
The period-four cat permits O(1/K) readout-angle changes to move O(1) parity
mass. A smooth/incoherent phase-intensity pushforward cannot be substituted.
No finite test can establish uniform asymptotics, a sampler, or advantage.

An optional parent theta-density envelope may support a coherent rejection
alternative, but the native kernel remains unpaid. For tau=beta+i alpha,
modular reduction to Im(tau')>=sqrt3/2 formally gives a Gaussian-periodic
majorant of |theta(z|tau)|^2. Sampling its integer residue index is cheap even
when the number of peaks is large. This is only a proposed subroutine; retain
interference between opposite phase branches and prove the Krawtchouk/caustic
transfer before using it. It is not the selected full CDF proof by itself.

## Current experiment and API work

Exact Sage control audits/controls/one_pulse_cdf/prefix_kernel.py checks
small native rotations, off-diagonal displacement, confluent diagonal, and
CDF identity. An initial Sage symbolic-to-QQbar coercion failed before tests;
explicit QQ normalization repaired it. Corrected run is pending; no result
is inferred. No quantum implementation or broad benchmark sweep.
Two distinct paid tasks will construct the full CDF compiler and attack its
uniform representation/near-revival clock. Reports remain advisory, no retries.


FILE: research/audits/api_inputs/2026-11-13-one-pulse/selection.md
# Post-Witt selection: native one-pulse Kerr CDF compilation

13 November 2026. Independent selection, not a new algorithm theorem.
STATE/TRAPS/GOAL read. Balanced expanded Witt is closed at its written scope;
no further field variant is selected. No network, API, Git, numerical tests,
archive reads, or shared-note edits were used in this pass.

## Decision and comparison boundary

Select one concrete classical attack on an already complete quantum endpoint:
**compile the coherent photon-count CDF for one binary-large Kerr pulse.**
The new operation is a Christoffel–Darboux/displacement reduction of the
number-prefix projector, followed by a possible certified theta-sum compiler.
It retains the off-diagonal interference which a phase-density pushforward loses.
This is preferable to another quantum access primitive: success would settle
the SAME full sampling law, while failure can identify a precise analytic cost.
No speedup, novelty, hardness, or classical match is asserted.

Three independent mechanisms were compared: compressed bosonic interference,
isogeny class actions, and topological braid evaluation. The latter two have
high external value, but the operations available here do not yet improve their
known mechanisms. They are rejected as next tasks, not declared impossible.

Corpus `been-tried` and `baselines` were run for:
- `one pulse binary Fock Kerr theta Krawtchouk`;
- `supersingular isogeny quantum walk nonbacktracking`, followed by the
  more specific `ordinary elliptic curve isogeny class group vectorization hidden shift`;
- `Jones polynomial plat closure link invariant normalization`.
Most hits were lexical and unrelated. No baseline-catalog hit for Kerr/Jones
is NOT evidence of absent classical algorithms. An additional shadow-Hamiltonian
comparison was discarded: the retained compendium itself requires a native
initial shadow state and invariant operator space, and notes the fixed-dimensional
light-cone limitation (physical LF2419–2501). That offers no new operation here.

## A. Selected: exact-law one-pulse Kerr sampling

**Native contract.** Binary K, two explicitly supplied rational-turn beam-splitter
angles theta1/theta2, an exact rational Kerr phase a/b, and TV tolerance epsilon.
Start at |K,0>; apply B(theta1), exp(2 pi i (a/b) binom(N,2)), B(theta2);
output the count j in {0,...,K}. Charge all angle bits, log(K+1), output bits,
and the requested error. No loss, smoothing, hidden repeat count, or phase oracle.
The complete quantum target poly(native bits,log(K+1),log(1/epsilon)) is already
written prior art, not the proposed contribution.

Actual retained primary statements read: Prakash et al., `binary_fock_kerr/prakash.txt`
LF844–898, Theorem2.2/Corollary2.3; Iyer et al., `iyer.txt` LF1363–1395,
Theorem4.2 including coherent Hermite phases and label cleanup. The native
cutoff/error composition is in `BINARY_FOCK_KERR_SAMPLING.md`.

**Strongest matched classical attacks.** Passive/bunched circuits are binomial;
terminal Kerr does not affect counts. The written coherent-branch sampler handles
one pulse in time polynomial in the NUMERICAL period 2b, and handles several
pulses in their product period. It already retains interference and finite-bit
clocks. Direct K+1 dimensional evolution and small tensor width remain valid.
Thus only genuinely large denominators/occupations need a new operation.
Rational approximation by itself does not remove numerical branch count.

### Exact reduction, independently derived

Let U be the real orthogonal number-basis matrix of B(theta2),
N=diag(0,...,K), Pi_r=diag(1_{j<=r}), P_r=U^T Pi_r U, and
w_n=exp(2 pi i (a/b) binom(n,2)) (B(theta1))_{n,K}.
The desired CDF is exactly F(r)=w^*P_r w. Put T=U N U^T.
The spin rotation gives a tridiagonal T; its adjacent entries have absolute
value |sin(theta2)cos(theta2)| sqrt((n+1)(K-n)). Its signs are fixed by U.
For 0<=r<K put t_r=T[r,r+1], u=U^T e_r, v=U^T e_{r+1}. Then

    [N,P_r] = U^T[T,Pi_r]U = t_r (v u^T-u v^T),
    P_r[n,m] = t_r (v_n u_m-u_n v_m)/(n-m),  n!=m.

This follows by multiplying the matrices: only the two entries crossing the
prefix boundary survive [T,Pi_r]. It is an exact identity at every K, angle,
phase, and prefix. P_K=I and P_{-1}=0 are separate exact endpoints.
The projector generally has rank r+1: **rank-two displacement is not low rank.**
When t_r=0 the rotated number measurement is diagonal/permuted and is elementary.

Hence a CDF evaluation consists of its diagonal contribution plus the explicit
bilinear Cauchy-kernel sum

    t_r sum_{n!=m} conjugate(w_n) w_m
                     (v_n u_m-u_n v_m)/(n-m).

The diagonal is NOT supplied by the commutator identity. In a Krawtchouk
polynomial normalization it is the confluent CD limit, involving derivatives;
its numerical compiler must be paid along with the off-diagonal expression.
The exact identity 1/h=(1/(2 pi)) integral_0^{2 pi} i(s-pi) exp(i h s) ds
for nonzero integer h turns the latter into a bilinear Fourier integral.
This is a useful target for a theta compiler, not an efficient quadrature proof.

### Why this operation would give the actual sampler

Suppose a deterministic compiler returns every F(r) to absolute error delta in
poly(log(K+1), angle bits, log(1/delta)) bit operations, uniformly in r.
Choose delta=epsilon/[8(K+1)] and a B-bit uniform variate with
2^-B<=epsilon/[8(K+1)]. Binary-search its quantile using these CDF values.
Couple with an exact uniform real variate. Unless that variate lies within
delta+2^-B of one of the K+1 true CDF boundaries, every comparison agrees with
the exact search. The bad set has measure at most
2(K+1)(delta+2^-B)<=epsilon/2. There are only ceil(log2(K+1))+1 queries.
No monotonicity of the approximations is needed on this good event.
This proves a fixed-clock TV sampler from that compiler; allocate any compiler
failure probability separately. Merely computing F to O(epsilon) gives a
Kolmogorov guarantee and does NOT establish TV sampling. The needed precision
still has only O(log(K+1)+log(1/epsilon)) bits.

### New source and exact remaining obligation

Actual Hiary, Annals2011, retained `2026-11-13-one-pulse/hiary_theta.txt`
LF62–95, Theorem1.1, computes
K^-j sum_{k=0}^K k^j exp(2 pi i (alpha k+beta k^2)) for REAL alpha,beta mod1.
Its arithmetic count and operand bits are polynomial in
(j+1)log(K/eta), with a stated polynomial prefactor in the error.
This really can remove numerical quadratic-sum length. It does NOT directly
cover Gaussian damping, Krawtchouk weights, the CD diagonal, or the bilinear
1/(n-m) expression. Those must be reduced to its actual input format.

The proposed constructive test is therefore precise: central binomial tail
control plus certified polynomial/oscillatory expansions of the two boundary
Krawtchouk functions, including their turning points, reducing BOTH CD pieces
to polynomially many Hiary calls and explicitly controlled bilinear integrals.
The number of pieces, polynomial degrees, coefficient sizes, cancellations,
precision and integration clocks must be polynomial in the charged parameters.
Growing K^c piece count, or an exponentially small normalization, defeats this
proposed compiler even though individual theta sums are fast.

The parent's modular continuous-theta rejection envelope is a possible
alternative subroutine. Even a proved constant rejection envelope there leaves
the native number-measurement kernel unpaid. It may be used in a coherent
two-branch envelope retaining the cross term; it may not replace amplitudes
by an incoherent phase mixture.

**Cheapest decisive stress cases.** Include balanced initial/readout rotations,
prefixes crossing a Krawtchouk turning point, and rational phases arbitrarily
near low-denominator revivals. The period-four Kerr cat has two opposite
equatorial condensates: a final O(1/K) rotation about their axis can change
their relative phase by O(1), hence count parity. A smooth phase-intensity
pushforward alone misses precisely this coherence. The existing branch method
handles the rational revival; a claimed uniform compiler must match it and
nearby phases without requiring numerical b or K work. Finite success would
not prove the uniform bounds; the exact CD identity is the starting certificate.

## B. Not selected: polynomial-time native isogeny vectorization

**Problem/value.** Public ordinary curves in a specified common-order class-action
instance; recover a verified connecting isogeny as a polynomial-size sequence
of small-degree maps. Any supplied order/action data must be part of the native
cryptographic contract, not hidden End/Hom advice. This concerns post-quantum
cryptography, independently of Kerr or quadratic-form transport.
**Proposed operation.** Compile a class/ideal description into a coherently
evaluable short smooth isogeny word, then exploit hidden translation.
**Goal/resources.** Poly(log q, public input,log(1/eta)) total time, including
class-group data, action evaluation, all walk steps and the actual output maps.
**Baseline/obligation.** The retained compendium LF993–1041 explicitly gives
only subexponential hidden-shift attacks, not a polynomial method. Efficient
action evaluation alone does not improve the hidden-shift measurement. A
binary exponent in a small-prime action is not a polylog-time isogeny walk.
Classical collision/smoothing attacks must be compared under the same order,
torsion data and output contract; SIDH breaks do not settle other contracts.
**Cheapest falsifier.** Count actual small-prime steps and source-state cost
before invoking an HSP clock; a superpolynomial word or untouched Kuperberg
stage rejects this proposed full clock. No new remedy for either is supplied.
Actual Childs–Jao–Soukharev (J. Math. Cryptology8,2014) is NOT retained/read here;
the compendium is a comparison lead, not a substitute primary theorem audit.
Do not fetch it merely to repeat a known hidden-shift wrapper.

## C. Not selected: native-scale Jones discrimination

**Problem/value.** Explicit braid word, nonexceptional fixed root of unity,
and additive inverse-polynomial accuracy for the ORIGINAL Jones value of its
trace closure. This is a topological invariant problem, not circuit acceptance
renamed as an application. Input crossings, strands and accuracy are charged.
**Proposed operation.** Coherent tangle/cap elimination with normalization
bookkeeping that avoids the exponentially scaled trace-accuracy requirement.
**Goal/resources.** Poly(crossings,strands,1/epsilon), including any postselection,
scalar normalizers, state preparation and finite-gate error.
**Baseline/obligation.** Skein contraction and bounded-width tensor/path-space
methods are the strongest immediate classical attacks on structured braids.
The compendium LF2999–3073 describes the known quantum approximation with
error epsilon |d|^(n-1) for trace closure, |d|=2cos(pi/k). This does not pay the
native-scale task. Its BQP/DQC1 statements do not fix this mismatch.
**Cheapest falsifier.** Repeated Markov stabilizations present the unknot with
growing strand count: its Jones value stays1 while its normalized trace has
magnitude |d|^(1-n). Thus a blanket inverse-polynomial normalized-signal premise
already fails on an easy family. This is not a lower bound for other algorithms.
No unitary normalization operation overcoming the cost is provided here.
Actual Aharonov–Jones–Landau primary source would be required before a new
normalization claim; the old local braid-HSP note's broad barriers are not used.

## Single next action and source needs

Attempt the native Kerr CDF compiler above, with two independent obligations:
construct a bounded representation of the full CD quadratic form, and attack
its uniform precision/turning-point/near-revival cost. Hiary's actual primary
text is already available. The useful remaining primary source is a complete
uniform Krawtchouk asymptotic/error theorem (including endpoint/coalescing saddles
and derivatives), or a direct derivation replacing it. An unread abstract or
the ordinary bulk two-saddle formula is insufficient. Do not start a quantum
implementation, benchmark sweep, or another arithmetic extension. A positive
result must output the native count law; a negative result must identify the
specific failed representation/clock and leave the full law unmatched.

# Binary-Fock Kerr circuits: prior-art endpoint and classical branch attack

7 November2026. CLOSED written quantum/classical composition with three
independent reviews read by the parent. Quantum endpoint is known prior art.
The bounded-branch bunched-input classical sampler is a written theorem,
not an implemented or executed sampler; exact finite controls are separate.

## Question, selection and native model

The question is whether binary-large occupation and a few non-Gaussian Kerr
phases give a sampling advantage after all access, cutoff and classical
baselines are charged. This is an end-to-end count-sampling problem, not a
new optical backend or a quantum-state preparation oracle.

Take0<epsilon<=1/4 without loss of generality. Input: m modes, binary nonnegative occupations n_i with total K, an explicit
list of L gates, and requested TV error epsilon. A gate is a two-mode passive
beam splitter B(theta)=exp(theta(a†b-b†a)), a number phase, or local Kerr
K_{a/b}=exp(2pi i (a/b) binom(n,2)), with rational angles in turns, binary
numerators/positive denominators. The desired output is one photon-count
vector distributed within epsilon of the ideal circuit. All input/angle
bits, list length, m and output m log(K+1) bits are charged. A stronger
unitary statement concerns arbitrary reference-entangled input of total K.
No squeezed/displaced input, loss, preparation oracle or binary-compressed
repeat count is included. L is the ACTUAL listed gate count.

The mechanism is common-grid quantum Hermite transforms around passive
optical operations, plus reversible modular arithmetic for Kerr phases.
Expected quantum target: poly(native bits, log(K+1), log(L/epsilon)) gates.
That target is already claimed by Prakash etal2610.03581v1 Corollary2.3:
this is PRIOR ART, not a new algorithm. The narrower number-conserving proof
below makes its native cutoff and coherent phase contract concrete.
No novelty, quantum/classical separation, practicality or execution claimed.

Before selection, corpus been-tried/baselines and actual primary literature
were checked for binary-spin/Krawtchouk, binary-Fock Kerr and bunched revival
sampling. The baseline catalog's irrelevant SDP hit is not a scientific
comparator. Current sparse-constant relations, growing-rank surface readout
and Gaudin-gap routes were independently compared: no paid constant map,
succinct cover readout or quantitative physical gap operation emerged.
A fixed-spectrum Cauchy Lax matrix admits spurious non-Bethe vectors and
therefore does not supply the Gaudin gap; no physical gap counterexample.

Strong classical comparators: explicit Fock evolution/permanent sampling,
small tensor width, Gaussian-positive-Wigner methods only on their genuine
state/measurement domain, bunched passive multinomial sampling, terminal
number-diagonal phases, and the coherent finite-branch sampler proved below.
A large bosonic Hilbert space is not evidence of hardness. Kerr Fourier
branches are coherent and cannot simply be classically mixed.

## 1. Paid known quantum endpoint

Actual sources retained under audits/sources/binary_fock_kerr/:
Iyer2602.15180v1 Lemma3.1, Theorem4.2 and its phase/label-erasure proof;
Prakash2610.03581v1 Theorems2.1/2.2 and Corollary2.3. Their PDFs, text and
SHA256 manifests are separate. This is a source-based written construction,
not independent execution of QHT or an independently implemented circuit.

Use one two-mode product QHT and operational grid for all local pair totals
at most K. Iyer Lemma3.1 uses the same discrete quadratic-chirp unitary on
each Fock input, with exponentially small grid error. Its proof accounts
for the high-energy intermediate SHEARS: only the complete beam splitter
conserves number, so a naive K truncation of every shear is invalid.
Theorem4.2 explicitly maps arbitrary superpositions and fixes Hermite phase
+1, then erases the occupation workspace coherently. Thus there is no
measurement or arbitrary fixed-spin-dependent phase. Source sign convention
requires exp(-2i theta A_12); Prakash BSY has the opposite sign.

There are d=(K+1)(K+2)/2 triangular two-mode input basis states. A common
per-column grid error delta gives restricted operator error<=sqrt(d)delta,
so delta=O(eta/(K+1)) pays all superpositions and references. Uniform QHT
operator errors telescope separately. The required grid size is polynomial
in K and1/eta, so its qubit count and the source gate cost remain polynomial
in log(K+1),log(1/eta). Choose one sufficiently padded cutoff/grid per gate.
If using the WHOLE rectangle n_a,n_b<=K, the inverse needs cutoff2K+1;
the native fixed-global-K proof only needs the triangle and cutoffK+1.

The original Hermite2510.04929 Theorem19 and Lemmas25--27 explicitly cover
coherent superpositions, a common amplification polynomial and degree-label
erasure. Pad its effective cutoff N_eff>=max(K+1,C log1/eta) to respect
N>log1/eta. Where the source bounds a squared tail bytau, use internal
tau=O(eta²). Both choices keep grid size polynomial and gate cost logarithmic
inK and1/eta. Its temporarily dropped(-1)^n Hermite convention must be
restored if needed; product parity commutes with a number-conserving mixer.

Reduce beam-splitter angles modulo2pi, never modulo pi while dropping
B(theta+pi)=(-1)^(n_a+n_b)B(theta). Local pair totals can be coherently
superposed even at fixed GLOBAL totalK. Number phases and Kerr phases are
computed by binary arithmetic; compute a*binom(n,2) mod b exactly, synthesize
the rational phase to eta and uncompute work. Exact modular arithmetic does
not mean arbitrary-angle synthesis is exact. All angle BIT lengths count.

Per-stage clean-isometry error O(epsilon/L) yields full errorO(epsilon) by
hybrid telescoping along the ideal total-K trajectory. Earlier digital
leakage is included in this operator error; no postselection or conditional
renormalization. Number measurement contracts trace distance. Map an invalid
padding tuple deterministically to the original valid input tuple; since
the ideal output is valid, this does not increase TV error. Initial binary
Fock preparation/output costO(m log(K+1)). K0 is trivial vacuum.

## 2. Exact interference and universality scope controls

Let K_pi(n)=exp(pi i binom(n,2)). It is1 on n0,1 and-1 on n2. For a balanced
B, the operation C=B†(K_pi tensor K_pi)B acts on the pair input states
00,10,01,11 as diag(1,1,1,-1), with zero leakage. In the two-photon sector
B|11> is a NOON state supported on20,02; both terms acquire-1. Total0/1
are unchanged. Apply this gadget between selected rails of two dual-rail
qubits. Native passive single-qubit rotations/phases plus this exact CZ
contain the usual universal gate set. Thus a general efficient classical
constant-TV sampler would simulate BQP sampling (and BQP decision with a
fixed sufficient error margin). This is a known-universality implication,
not proof BPP!=BQP, sampling hardness, novelty or an exponential separation.
It already uses small occupations and does not arise from high K alone.

For K_pi, period4 Fourier coefficients are
    c=(0,(1-i)/2,0,(1+i)/2),
    K_pi(n)=sum_r c_r exp(2pi i r n/4).
An exact two-photon witness is
    |20> -> B(pi/4) -> K_pi on modea -> B(pi/8)†.
Its output is -|11>, hence counts(0,1,0) in basis(02,11,20). The incoherent
Fourier mixture instead has probabilities(1/4,1/2,1/4), TVdistance1/2.
A spectator-mode control keeps globaltotal1 while pairtotals0,1 are
superposed; reducing B(pi) toidentity makes the two final states orthogonal.

These identities are frozen in audits/controls/binary_fock_kerr/control.py
and result.json using exact Sage algebraic arithmetic. They do not execute
QHT, prove the large-K gate bound or establish complexity separation.

## 3. Constructive classical branch sampler

Restrict only this CLASSICAL theorem to a bunched input |K,0,...,0> (the
occupied mode can be specified). Keep arbitrary passive gates and rational
Kerr gates. For Kerr j choose q_j=2b_j after fraction reduction; an identity
phase may useq_j1. The exact period dividesq_j. Fourier expansion gives

    K_j(n)=sum_(r<q_j) c_jr exp(2pi i r n/q_j),
    c_jr=q_j^-1 sum_(u<q_j) K_j(u) exp(-2pi i r u/q_j),
    sum_r |c_jr|²=1.

After expanding t Kerr gates there are chi=product_j q_j indexed branches.
Each branch is an ordinary passive interferometer U_r with coefficientc_r,
where sum_r |c_r|²=1 even if some branches coincide. The actual state is
Phi=sum_r c_r psi_r and has norm1 because the original circuit is unitary.
Here psi_r is a normalized bosonic condensate with one-particle vector
alpha_r=U_r e_input. Its count amplitude is exactly

    psi_r(x)=sqrt(K!/product_i x_i!) product_i alpha_ri^(x_i), sum_i x_i=K.

Its probabilities are multinomial, efficiently sampled by m-1 BINOMIAL
samples with binary totals. Its complex amplitude, including signs/phases,
can be evaluated to polynomial requested BIT precision with logfactorials
and binary angle multiplication; it is not a permanent of sizeK.

Choose a branch uniformly from the chi indices, then sample x from its
multinomial law. The proposal is p(x)=S(x)/chi, S=sum_r |psi_r(x)|². Accept
with probability
    A(x)=|sum_r c_r psi_r(x)|²/S(x).
Cauchy-Schwarz and sum|c|²1 imply0<=A<=1. The accepted distribution is
EXACTLY the desired count law, with acceptanceprobability1/chi. This
retains interference; it is not the incorrect Fourier mixture in section2.
Finite numerical normalization is paid below. Runtime polynomial in chi,
m,L, nativebitlength,log(K+1),log(1/epsilon); hence polynomial in nativebits
when chi is polynomial. An exponentially large chi is charged, not ignored.
Constantly many low-denominator Kerr phases are a natural covered case.
The universality gadget has chi exponential in the number of nonlinear gates,
so this classical theorem does not dequantize all native circuits.
